steps: Rinse the poha in a strainer two or three times, drain and leave 5 minutes, until a flake crushes easily between your fingers.
Sprinkle the salt, sugar and turmeric over it and mix lightly with your fingers.
Heat the oil on medium and fry the peanuts until golden and crunchy, then lift them out onto a plate.
In the same oil let the mustard seeds pop, then add the cumin, hing and curry leaves for a few seconds.
Add the onion and green chilli and fry on medium for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion is soft and see-through.
Add the small potato cubes, cover and cook on low for about 8 minutes, stirring once or twice, until a cube mashes easily.
Add the poha and peanuts, toss gently, cover and steam on very low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot.
Turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot.
note: Curry leaves and fried peanuts are now in, as every Maharashtrian kanda poha has them; peanuts are 10 g a plate, between the two sources. Potato is cut to 50 g so the onion stays the star, and the optional grated coconut is left out.
